chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAmr, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning:

Regarding a man who urinates, then performs istinja', then afterward finds moisture, he said: If, after urinating, he draws his hand from between the anus and the testicles three times, and presses what is between them, then performs istinja', then if something flows out until it reaches the shanks, he should not be concerned.

key_terms.فَخَرَطَ: he draws or wipes with pressure along the passage
key_terms.فَلَا يُبَالِي: he should not be concerned or pay attention to it
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: he performs istinja', cleansing the private part after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man finds moisture after urinating and performing istinja'?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about moisture found after urination and the method of preventing doubt through a particular cleansing practice before istinja'. It indicates that if a man performs this procedure and then later finds discharged moisture, he should not be concerned by it.
